title: Academic Core
description: Build accurate, usable vocabulary for academic core.

items.definition_en: a typical model or pattern of thought
items.example: The findings challenge the dominant paradigm.

items.definition_en: a standard used to make a judgement
items.example: Cost should not be the sole criterion.

items.definition_en: existing as a natural or permanent quality
items.example: Uncertainty is inherent in long-term forecasts.

items.definition_en: logical and internally consistent
items.example: The essay develops a coherent argument.

title: High-value IELTS Verbs
description: Build accurate, usable vocabulary for high-value ielts verbs.

items.definition_en: to make a problem more severe
items.example: Poor planning may exacerbate housing shortages.

items.definition_en: to reduce the harmful effect of something
items.example: Green spaces can mitigate urban heat.

items.definition_en: to make an action or process easier
items.example: Public investment can facilitate innovation.

items.definition_en: to gradually weaken something
items.example: Misinformation can undermine public trust.

title: High-value IELTS Adjectives
description: Build accurate, usable vocabulary for high-value ielts adjectives.

items.definition_en: spreading widely through an area or group
items.example: Digital technology has a pervasive influence.

items.definition_en: causing harm or damage
items.example: Long commutes are detrimental to well-being.

items.definition_en: possible and practical to achieve
items.example: The proposal is financially feasible.

items.definition_en: open to more than one interpretation
items.example: The survey question was ambiguous.

title: Academic Nouns
description: Build accurate, usable vocabulary for academic nouns.

items.definition_en: a likely effect or meaning
items.example: The policy has major implications for schools.

items.definition_en: general agreement among a group
items.example: There is broad consensus on the need for reform.

items.definition_en: a factor that limits action
items.example: Time was the main constraint on the research.

items.definition_en: a noticeable and often unfair difference
items.example: The data reveals a regional disparity in income.

title: Collocations for Argumentation
description: Build accurate, usable vocabulary for collocations for argumentation.

items.definition_en: a strongly persuasive set of reasons
items.example: The evidence makes a compelling case for intervention.

items.definition_en: an incorrect basis for an argument
items.example: The conclusion follows from a flawed premise.

items.definition_en: to respond to a claim with opposing reasons
items.example: Recent evidence counters the argument effectively.

items.definition_en: to support a statement with evidence
items.example: The author fails to substantiate the claim.

title: Cause and Effect Vocabulary
description: Build accurate, usable vocabulary for cause and effect vocabulary.

items.definition_en: to cause something to happen
items.example: Rapid migration can give rise to housing pressure.

items.definition_en: to be caused by something
items.example: The decline stems from weak demand.

items.definition_en: one cause among several
items.example: Poor maintenance was a contributing factor.

items.definition_en: an indirect result caused by an earlier event
items.example: Fuel prices have a knock-on effect on food costs.

title: Comparison Vocabulary
description: Build accurate, usable vocabulary for comparison vocabulary.

items.definition_en: similar enough to allow comparison
items.example: The two samples are broadly comparable.

items.definition_en: used to show a clear difference
items.example: In contrast to cities, rural areas lost population.

items.definition_en: in the same order as previously mentioned
items.example: The figures were 40 and 55 percent, respectively.

items.definition_en: to be greater or more important than
items.example: The long-term benefits outweigh the initial costs.

title: Trend and Change Vocabulary
description: Build accurate, usable vocabulary for trend and change vocabulary.

items.definition_en: to rise and fall irregularly
items.example: Oil prices fluctuated throughout the period.

items.definition_en: to stop increasing after a period of growth
items.example: Demand plateaued at around 60 percent.

items.definition_en: a clear and significant reduction
items.example: The chart shows a marked decline in exports.

items.definition_en: increasing through small regular steps
items.example: The programme delivered incremental improvements.

title: Problem and Solution Vocabulary
description: Build accurate, usable vocabulary for problem and solution vocabulary.

items.definition_en: to take action concerning a problem
items.example: The strategy addresses the issue of affordability.

items.definition_en: an answer that can work successfully
items.example: Public transport offers a viable solution.

items.definition_en: the fundamental origin of a problem
items.example: Enforcement alone ignores the root cause.

items.definition_en: an action intended to correct harm
items.example: The agency introduced a remedial measure.

title: Policy Vocabulary
description: Build accurate, usable vocabulary for policy vocabulary.

items.definition_en: government action intended to change an outcome
items.example: Targeted policy intervention reduced child poverty.

items.definition_en: the system of rules governing an activity
items.example: A clear regulatory framework encourages investment.

items.definition_en: money spent by government
items.example: Public expenditure on health increased.

items.definition_en: to make sure a law or rule is obeyed
items.example: Authorities must enforce safety standards.

title: Education
description: Build accurate, usable vocabulary for education.

items.definition_en: fair access to learning opportunities
items.example: Funding reform may improve educational equity.

items.definition_en: a test administered under consistent conditions
items.example: Standardised assessment enables broad comparison.

items.definition_en: the process of gaining knowledge
items.example: Active practice supports knowledge acquisition.

items.definition_en: education after secondary school
items.example: Participation in tertiary education has expanded.

title: Environment
description: Build accurate, usable vocabulary for environment.

items.definition_en: the environmental impact of a person or activity
items.example: Public transport reduces a city's ecological footprint.

items.definition_en: the use of resources faster than replacement
items.example: Overconsumption accelerates resource depletion.

items.definition_en: responsible protection of the natural world
items.example: Schools can promote environmental stewardship.

items.definition_en: producing a large amount of carbon emissions
items.example: Heavy industry remains carbon-intensive.

title: Technology
description: Build accurate, usable vocabulary for technology.

items.definition_en: loss of jobs caused by new technology
items.example: Automation may cause technological displacement.

items.definition_en: guided by the analysis of data
items.example: Hospitals increasingly use data-driven decisions.

items.definition_en: ability to use digital tools effectively
items.example: Digital literacy is essential in modern workplaces.

items.definition_en: close monitoring of people or activity
items.example: Facial recognition enables extensive surveillance.

title: Health
description: Build accurate, usable vocabulary for health.

items.definition_en: a measurable result of healthcare or behaviour
items.example: Early treatment improves the health outcome.

items.definition_en: an illness that continues for a long time
items.example: Diabetes is a common chronic condition.

items.definition_en: the overall impact of disease on society
items.example: Smoking creates a substantial public health burden.

items.definition_en: an avoidable difference in health between groups
items.example: Rural communities face a persistent health disparity.

title: Society
description: Build accurate, usable vocabulary for society.

items.definition_en: the strength of relationships within society
items.example: Shared public spaces support social cohesion.

items.definition_en: a change in the structure of a population
items.example: Ageing represents a major demographic shift.

items.definition_en: movement between social or economic positions
items.example: Education can promote social mobility.

items.definition_en: treatment of a group as unimportant
items.example: Language barriers can deepen marginalisation.

title: Economics
description: Build accurate, usable vocabulary for economics.

items.definition_en: ability to recover from economic shocks
items.example: Diverse industries strengthen economic resilience.

items.definition_en: government decisions about taxation and spending
items.example: Fiscal policy can stimulate demand.

items.definition_en: the amount that money can buy
items.example: Inflation erodes household purchasing power.

items.definition_en: inefficient distribution of goods by a market
items.example: Pollution is often treated as a market failure.

title: Cities
description: Build accurate, usable vocabulary for cities.

items.definition_en: a city's ability to withstand disruption
items.example: Flood planning improves urban resilience.

items.definition_en: housing reasonably priced for local incomes
items.example: The city faces a shortage of affordable housing.

items.definition_en: development combining homes, shops, and services
items.example: Mixed-use development can shorten daily journeys.

items.definition_en: the quality of a place as somewhere to live
items.example: Green space improves urban liveability.

title: Government
description: Build accurate, usable vocabulary for government.

items.definition_en: an institution's ability to perform effectively
items.example: Reform depends on sufficient institutional capacity.

items.definition_en: public acceptance of democratic authority
items.example: Transparency strengthens democratic legitimacy.

items.definition_en: consistency among different public policies
items.example: Cross-agency planning improves policy coherence.

items.definition_en: public involvement in community and government
items.example: Local forums encourage civic participation.

title: Research and Science
description: Build accurate, usable vocabulary for research and science.

items.definition_en: careful and exact use of research methods
items.example: The trial demonstrates methodological rigour.

items.definition_en: evaluation of research by experts
items.example: The paper underwent independent peer review.

items.definition_en: a conclusion that one factor causes another
items.example: The small sample limits causal inference.

items.definition_en: a result that remains valid under scrutiny
items.example: The association appears to be a robust finding.

title: Lexical Precision
description: Build accurate, usable vocabulary for lexical precision.

items.definition_en: to support a statement with additional evidence
items.example: Later studies corroborate the initial result.

items.definition_en: to argue that a claim is true
items.example: Critics contend that the reform is premature.

items.definition_en: occurring at irregular intervals
items.example: The region experienced sporadic rainfall.

items.definition_en: very great or far-reaching
items.example: Migration had a profound social impact.

title: Paraphrasing
description: Build accurate, usable vocabulary for paraphrasing.

items.definition_en: to form a proportion or explain a result
items.example: Transport accounts for a third of emissions.

items.definition_en: to serve as a sign of something
items.example: The decline may be indicative of lower demand.

items.definition_en: a notably large share of a whole
items.example: A considerable proportion chose public transport.

items.definition_en: to experience a major change
items.example: The district underwent a rapid transformation.

title: Register and Formality
description: Build accurate, usable vocabulary for register and formality.

items.definition_en: despite what has just been stated
items.example: The sample was small; nevertheless, the pattern was clear.

items.definition_en: concerning a particular subject
items.example: With regard to cost, the second option is preferable.

items.definition_en: used to identify an important observation
items.example: It is noteworthy that participation doubled.

items.definition_en: an issue that causes justified worry
items.example: Air quality remains a matter of concern.
